SMTO-CMP-0010 — The AI's claimed result doesn't match what SMTO saw

GUID: 26a489e0-cac9-4264-82e7-d8cf03503a3c
Slug: completion-check-mismatch
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • The AI model said a result had a certain value, but the saved output shows something different. SMTO won't accept a claim that disagrees with what was actually seen. Work already done is kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details in this panel and the task's steps to compare what the AI claimed with what SMTO actually saw. Seeing both shows whether the AI misreported the result or the work isn't finished.
  2. Check the real system yourself to see which value is correct. The saved output may be out of date, or the AI may have misread it.
  3. Tell SMTO what you found in the "Continue this conversation" box under the task and select Continue, or select Resume to let it recheck. SMTO then corrects its claim or does only the missing work, without repeating finished steps.
  4. Don't select Restart task while you're unsure what already happened. Restart begins a fresh attempt and doesn't undo earlier actions, so changes could happen twice.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Completed and its reply matches the value you checked.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, with the value you saw yourself. Check whether the earlier action already happened before anything is repeated. Don't restart the task while that is unclear.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A completion check's JSON pointer resolved in the cited receipt, but the observed value differs from the declared equals value under canonical JSON comparison (reason check_mismatch).

What this means

  • An exact JSON-pointer check resolves an observed value but canonical JSON comparison differs from the declared equals value. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • An exact JSON-pointer check resolves an observed value but canonical JSON comparison differs from the declared equals value.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the observed/expected values and any literal-newline mismatch without changing a caller requirement to hide failure.

How to fix it

  • Compare expected and observed (and literal_newline_escape_mismatch for strings) in the requirement attached to the run's completion.rejected event (check_observations in src/agent_runtime/native/completion.py). Correct an optional model claim to the observed value, or satisfy a required caller check with a new current observation; never change a caller requirement to hide the failure.
  • Read the current check value and correct the completion claim to match the observed result.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • A corrected optional claim or newly satisfied real requirement agrees with authoritative observation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors
